headline: Minomeet: The Zero-Bot, 100% Private AI Meeting Copilot built with React & Node.js
summary: Minomeet AI automates meeting summaries, decisions, and action items in minutes. It ensures 100% privacy by processing audio locally, eliminating the need for external bots.
details: Minomeet AI is an open-source, autonomous meeting intelligence copilot designed to eliminate post-meeting administrative work. It transforms long conversations into structured Executive Summaries, Key Decision matrices, Action Items, and follow-up emails in just 2-5 minutes.

Unlike most AI notetakers that rely on external cloud bots joining calendar invites, Minomeet ensures 100% privacy. It achieves this by using native Dual-Channel Audio Ingestion directly on your machine, keeping all data local.

Engineered as a unified, full-stack TypeScript application, Minomeet can be run locally using Docker or standard Node.js. All meeting data and audio uploads are automatically stored in persistent Docker volumes, giving users full control.

Minomeet is released under the MIT License, making it freely available for teams managing meetings, sales demos, or daily standups. Developers are encouraged to give it a try and support ongoing local AI development by starring the project on GitHub.

headline: Apple tells Mac App Store developers they can now drop Intel support
summary: Mac App Store developers can now drop Intel support for universal macOS apps that require macOS 13 or later, marking a significant step in Apple's transition to Apple Silicon.
details: Apple is now allowing developers to drop Intel support for universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store. This applies specifically to apps that require macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, pushing forward the full transition to Apple Silicon.

This policy change means developers no longer need to include Intel x86_64 architecture binaries in their app bundles for these newer macOS versions. This can result in smaller app sizes and streamlined development for Apple Silicon-native applications.

The move follows Apple's multi-year transition away from Intel processors, which began with the introduction of its M-series chips in 2020. This further solidifies the company's commitment to its proprietary silicon architecture.
caption:
Mac App Store developers can now officially drop Intel support for their apps.

Apple is now allowing developers to drop Intel support for universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store. This applies specifically to apps that require macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, pushing forward the full transition to Apple Silicon.

This policy change means developers no longer need to include Intel x86_64 architecture binaries in their app bundles for these newer macOS versions. This can result in smaller app sizes and streamlined development for Apple Silicon-native applications.

The move follows Apple's multi-year transition away from Intel processors, which began with the introduction of its M-series chips in 2020. This further solidifies the company's commitment to its proprietary silicon architecture.
